subject: Use when discovering a domain through events, commands, actors, policies, aggregates, read models, external systems,…

evals.prompt: Define event-storming in 2-3 sentences. Include the work it owns and the kind of user request that should activate it.
Explain why an agent would need the event-storming skill instead of relying on generic reasoning. Name the failure it prevents.
Describe the mental model or main primitives behind event-storming. Keep it operational rather than just naming the topic.
A user asks: "implement Shopify webhook signature verification and idempotent retries". Should event-storming activate? Explain the boundary and name the better owner when possible.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not force event-storming onto a request it explicitly excludes or that belongs to system-interface-contracts, webhook-integration, api-design, bounded-context-mapping, state-machine-modeling, event-contract-design, conceptual-modeling, data-modeling.

evals.prompt: A user asks: "map the order lifecycle as domain events before we design tables or APIs". Show the first concrete steps an agent should take when applying event-storming.

Place event-storming among its adjacent skills (system-interface-contracts, webhook-integration, api-design, bounded-context-mapping, state-machine-modeling, event-contract-design, conceptual-modeling, data-modeling). What does it own, and what does it verify with or defer to?
evals.negative_expectation: Must not collapse related skills into interchangeable names; ownership must be mechanism-level.

evals.prompt: Name one plausible misconception about event-storming and correct it with a mechanism-level explanation.
